thesis: Arista Networks is the leading merchant-silicon data-center Ethernet switching vendor and a core beneficiary of the AI back-end networking build-out as hyperscalers standardize AI clusters on Ethernet rather than InfiniBand. Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $3.04B with Q3 2026 guidance near $3.3B and FY2026 revenue guidance lifted to ~$12.6B (~40% YoY). TTM EPS is roughly $3.50, implying a ~54x P/E at $188.67 — a full valuation near 52-week highs after a strong run. The long-term AI networking tailwind is intact, but the stock now prices in much of the near-term upside, so we rate it HOLD and would wait for a better entry. Key risks are customer concentration (Microsoft/Meta historically), competition from Cisco/Nvidia/InfiniBand, and white-box alternatives.

drivers: AI back-end Ethernet revenue accelerates beyond the ~$12.6B FY2026 guide as hyperscalers expand clusters and Arista captures 800G/1.6T upgrades
FY2026 revenue reaches or exceeds ~$12.6B and operating margins stay above 40%, supporting a premium multiple
Campus/enterprise diversification reduces cloud-customer concentration faster than expected
Competitive fears around Cisco/Nvidia/InfiniBand fade and Arista sustains share gains in cloud switching

base_case.assumptions: Arista delivers FY2026 revenue near the ~$12.6B guidance range with ~25–30% YoY growth, gross margins in the low-to-mid 60s, and operating margins around 40%. The market applies a ~50–55x multiple on ~$3.50–$3.75 TTM EPS, leaving the stock near current levels over the next 12–18 months.

risks: Hyperscaler AI capex digestion or a Microsoft/Meta spending pause cuts orders and compresses the premium multiple
White-box or in-house switching programs at the largest cloud customers erode Arista's share
Nvidia's InfiniBand/Spectrum-X or Cisco's Silicon One win more AI back-end sockets
A broad semiconductor/AI de-rating or tariff shock hits high-beta networking names

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings reported — revenue ~$3.04B, Q3 guidance ~$3.3B, FY2026 guidance raised to ~$12.6B
Q3 results and updated Q4/FY2026 outlook; AI networking mix and margin trajectory
Full-year FY2026 results and initial FY2027 revenue framework
800G/1.6T Ethernet design wins and hyperscaler AI cluster deployments

key_risks: Customer concentration: historically large revenue share from Microsoft and Meta; any shift to in-house or white-box switching would be material
Valuation: ~54x TTM P/E near 52-week highs prices in strong execution and limits near-term upside
Competition: Cisco, Nvidia (InfiniBand/Spectrum-X), and Broadcom-based white-box alternatives compete for AI/cloud networking budgets
AI capex cycle: a hyperscaler spending pause or ROI-driven digestion would hit orders and sentiment
Macro/geopolitical: tariffs, supply-chain constraints, and export controls could pressure margins and lead times
